tweets:
We added retries to our payment API.

Customer support started getting emails about duplicate charges.

Different bug a week later: SQS redelivered a message and users got two welcome emails.

Same root cause: we assumed work happens once. It doesn't. 🧵

Idempotent = run it 5 times, same effect as once.

Natural:
• UPDATE email = X
• DELETE /resource/99

Not natural:
• POST /orders
• charge $50
• sendWelcomeEmail()

Retries + at-least-once delivery WILL duplicate. Design for it.

Idempotency keys fix non-idempotent mutations.

Client: one key per checkout click, reuse on retry.
Server: store key + result; duplicate key → replay response, NO second charge.

Stripe's Idempotency-Key header is the pattern. Unique DB constraint prevents concurrent double-charge races.

Delivery guarantees:

• At-most-once → can LOSE messages
• At-least-once → can DUPLICATE (SQS default)
• Exactly-once → hard; usually "at-least-once + idempotent consumer"

There is no middleware toggle that removes duplicates without app-level dedup.

Dual write problem:

db.insert(order) ✅
queue.publish(event) ❌

→ order exists, downstream never notified.

Outbox pattern: insert order + outbox row in ONE transaction. Relay publishes from outbox. Consumers still idempotent — relay retries too.
